messages:
Maya S.: Heads-up — support ticket #SR-4821 from AcmeRetail. They sent a batch rerank request with 2 queries and 3 candidates each, but results look like candidates are misaligned across queries. Customer reports candidate IDs from the second query appearing under the first query's scores.

Ethan R.: Can you paste a minimal repro (request + response) and whether they're using any multiplex/compact headers or a new client?

Maya S.: Pasting minimal stripped payload from customer:
```json
{
  "queries": ["what is return policy?","nearest store hours"],
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"30 day returns"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"returns accepted"},
    {"id":"c3","text":"no returns"},
    {"id":"c4","text":"store hours 9-9"},
    {"id":"c5","text":"open 10-8"},
    {"id":"c6","text":"holiday hours"}
  ],
  "per_query_candidates": [3,3]
}
```
Customer says they used endpoint `POST /v1/rerank/batch` and got back scores where c4-c6 were mapped to query1, etc.

Priya K.: Interesting — the runtime recently added an optimization for multiplexing that accepts a flat `candidates` array + `per_query_candidates` counts and reconstructs per-query buckets. If `X-Multiplex-Mode: true` header is set we treat it as flat input. Any chance their client/library set the header? Also saw a change in PR #1209 where we introduced `compact_candidates` path.

Maya S.: Customer attached their request headers: `Authorization: Bearer xxxx`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Multiplex-Mode: true`. They didn't realize the header would change behavior.

Ethan R.: Repro locally by toggling header.

LogCollectorBot: Pasted log snippet from a repro run:
```
INFO 2025-12-08T13:22:11Z rerank-service handler: received batch size=2 candidates_total=6 multiplex=true
WARN 2025-12-08T13:22:11Z rerank-service mapper: per_query_counts present [3,3] but codepath fell back to legacy offset parsing
ERROR 2025-12-08T13:22:11Z rerank-service result-mapping: mapping mismatch: assigned_indices=[0,1,2,0,1,2]
```

Priya K.: Looks like a regression: when both `per_query_candidates` and `compact_candidates` feature flags are present, mapping uses modulo arithmetic instead of slicing. That explains why c4 got assigned to index 0 of the first query.

Ethan R.: Quick workaround for the customer: remove `X-Multiplex-Mode` header or use nested `candidates` arrays (i.e., `candidates: [[...],[...]]`) until we ship a fix.

Maya S.: Customer removed the header and confirmed scores realign. They see expected top candidate per query now.

Priya K.: I'll open a patch — change the mapping logic in `multiplex_mapper.cpp` to use prefix sums with explicit slicing and validate `sum(per_query_candidates) == len(candidates)`. Add unit tests for edge cases (zero candidates, uneven sums, large batch sizes).

DeployBot: Patch merged to main, CI green. Rolling to canary (3 nodes) in us-west-2 now.

Ethan R.: ETA to full rollout?

DeployBot: Canary healthy after 10m, rolling to remaining nodes, expected complete in 45m. Will post when done.

Maya S.: Thanks team — I'll update SR-4821 with repro steps and the workaround.

LogCollectorBot: Final note from post-deploy check:
```
INFO mapping checker: per_query_counts [3,3] candidates_total 6 mapping verified
```

Maya S.: Marking resolved — customer happy. :tada:
